title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-04
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality soundboard recording of a solid set with standout Hard To Handle, China Rider and Black Peter, but plagued by hiss, cuts and a wobbling Midnight Hour.
ai_review.review: The Kaplan SBD source captures an intriguing early‑70 show that delivers strong performances – a smoking Hard To Handle, an exploratory China Rider and a beautifully sung Black Peter – while the jam after Midnight gets mixed reactions.  The audio is noticeably garbled, hissy and occasionally cuts, which keeps the listening experience from being pristine but still enjoyable for fans of the era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical moments (show quality ~4/5) while consistently noting recording flaws that keep technical quality around fair (~3/5). Weighted combination yields a solid above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy, garbled and sometimes distorted with audible cuts and buzzing; acceptable for 1970 standards but far from pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set builds nicely with tight early songs, a strong jam after Midnight, and an especially good China Rider; however the Midnight Hour drags for some listeners, leaving the overall flow solid but not spectacular.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Solo work described as "gliding over tribal funk" and his vocal delivery on Black Peter praised as a top performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh's bass noted for laying it down with Santana‑style percussion during the post‑Midnight jam.
